title: Digital F(r)ictions
description: Digital F(r)ictions is a research-creation project selected for MAMBO’s Digital Residency, organized by the Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá. Developed together the Digital Visual Studies team, the project uses artificial intelligence to explore and reinterpret Bogotá through the lens of the museum’s digital collection. By analyzing visual and textual features from artworks, the project constructs new artistic and urban narratives, offering critical reflections on both the city and the role of AI in cultural institutions. The initiative merges curatorial practice with machine learning, re-signifying the MAMBO Collection while addressing ethical and cultural dimensions of digital technologies.

title: Fly-Meet
description: Fly&Meet is a non-profit project that provides a platform to find affordable shared destinations among multiple origins. People from different places find the most comfortable destination for both parties. Technically, it leverages the Kiwi API to make multi-origins flights search and filters the results to show the cumulatively cheapest destinations.  Interestingly, the platform reveals the hidden geography of the aerial network where the most affordable destinations between two nodes might fall far from their middle location.

title: 3D Visibility study
description: Result of a collaboration with the italian mobility firm Systematica, the web-app functions as a data-visualization platform for the stakeholders involved in the Scalo Porta Romana project in Milan. It showcases several layers of a three dimensional visibility study. Rather than a simple report, the platform permits an active interaction with the data, which remains queriable to filters and selections. In this manner, actors involved in the development process used the platform to discuss the positioning of emergency signs, benches, and other visibility-dependant amenities.

title: Multipli(city)
description: Halfway between a mental map and an index, the multipli-city navigator collects the outputs of a PhD seminar led by D. Negueruela del Castillo, G. Savicic and I.Neri at EPFL, Lausanne. Leveraging the powerful open-source Leaflet and the minimal Alpine JS packages, it permits a twofold reading of its content in the form of pamphlets and conceptual diagrams spatially placed in a fictitious geography

title: Cities Matchmaking
description: Cities Matchmaking is a platform to inspect the results of the homonym publication developed together with Erze Dinarama for the opening chapter of The Routledge Handbook on Greening High-Density Cities edited by Peng Du, Kheir Al-Kodmany, Mir M. Ali. The visualization shows in an interactive fashion the study carried out on a set of global cities  (approx 4500) in the search of ecological twins to support international collaboration projects in the face of climate changes. More precisely, the research produces 7 map indicators for every city, later analyzed for similarity via Machine Learning algorithms.

title: Emerging Assemblages
description: Emerging Assemblages: Navigating Shifting Ecologies is a digital platform that will accompany the Kosovo Pavilion at the Venice Biennale 2025. The website will serve as a dynamic space to explore the themes and narratives presented in the pavilion. More specifically, the pavilion explores shifting seasonal patterns and ecological disruptions, particularly in relation to agricultural change and species migration.

title: Itzal
description: Awarded best idea at the Basque government’s open data contest (2022), Itzal - or “Shadow” in Euskara - is a routing web app to fight the harsh spanish summer sun. It allows users to see pathways that minimize exposure to sun at different times of the day. Thanks to this alternative route, users can reduce risk to sun heat and high temperatures in order to avoid possible dizziness, sunstroke and heat stroke and improve the experience of active and healthy mobility throughout summer. Technically it exploits a mix of 3D modeling and climatic forecasting to evaluate ad-hoc shortest paths over a road graph.
